title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the step after the list of questions on p.11 (a)–(d), which ask whether 'structures a), b)' form stacks, whether the functor to crystals is faithful, and whether one can attach a finite locally free group scheme to (ω, F_ω, V_ω). Here Grothendieck specialises to truncated Barsotti–Tate groups of level 1 (BT_1) over a base S of characteristic p.

Notation, in modern terms:
- 𝓜 is the Dieudonné crystal of G and M its value on S (the page writes M = ε*(𝓜)).
- φ is the absolute Frobenius of S, with φ*(M) = M^(p).
- F: M^(p) → M and V: M → M^(p) are the Frobenius and Verschiebung.
- Data b) is the co-Lie complex ℓ. of G and the complex ℓ.' of the dual. For a BT_1 in characteristic p the differential of ℓ. vanishes, so H^0 and H^{-1} are locally free of the same rank.
- Being BT_1 means Ker F = Im V and Ker V = Im F, on the crystal and hence on M.

Step 1 (taking H^1). Data b) gives the Hodge filtration 0 → ω → M → ν' → 0, with ω = H^0(ℓ.) = ω_G and ν' = H^1(ℓ.'^∨) the Lie algebra of the dual, both locally free. After Frobenius pullback, φ*(ω) = Im(V: M → M^(p)). This is the classical 'Frobenius twist of the Hodge filtration equals Im V = Ker F' (cf. Oda, Mazur).

Step 2 (taking H^0). Similarly 0 → n → M → t' → 0 with n = H^{-1}(ℓ.), t' = H^0(ℓ.'^∨), and φ*(n) = Ker(F: M^(p) → M).

Step 3. Since Ker F = Im V, φ*(n) = φ*(ω). He concludes n = ω and t' = ν'. The margin note reads: 'this determines ω uniquely!'

Step 4. Can (𝓜, F, V) alone recover all of data b)? He shows that the induced semilinear operators come for free:
- V_ω: ω → ω^(p) is the restriction of V to ω, landing in ω^(p) = Im V.
- F_{t'}: t'^(p) → t'. Since t'^(p) = Coker V and FV = 0, F factors through Coker V = t'^(p). By Ker F = Im V this gives an injection t'^(p) ↪ M; composing with M → t' gives F_{t'}.
- Dually, ω' = t'^∨ with V_{ω'} = ^tF_{t'}.

Continuation (p.13). He assembles a 'cross' diagram: the Hodge filtration 0 → ω → M → t' → 0, and the conjugate filtration 0 → t'^(p) --F--> M --V--> ω^(p) → 0. In modern terms, a BT_1 yields a locally free M with two filtrations (Hodge and conjugate) and Frobenius-linear identifications of their graded pieces. That is precisely an F-zip in the sense of Moonen–Wedhorn (2004).

Purpose. To test whether BT_1's in characteristic p over general bases are classified by such linear-algebra data (questions c) and d) of p.11), as part of Grothendieck's Dieudonné-crystal programme (Montréal 1970).
errors: The inference φ*(n) = φ*(ω) ⇒ n = ω (and the margin claim 'cela détermine ω de façon unique') needs Frobenius pullback to detect equality of locally direct summands. That holds if φ is faithfully flat, e.g. S regular (Kunz), or more generally S reduced with flat Frobenius. It fails over non-reduced bases: over S = Spec k[ε], φ* factors through k, so φ*(ω) only sees ω mod ε. The Hodge filtration is then not determined by (M, F, V); its freedom is exactly what Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory parametrises.

In the BT_1 case n ≅ ω already holds intrinsically, since the co-Lie complex has zero differential in characteristic p. So the real content is the equality n = ω as submodules of M, and that is subject to the caveat above.
Notation slips between M and 𝓜 (ε* vs φ*) make it unclear whether M is the crystal's value on S or a Frobenius descent. The argument as written only makes sense with M^(p) = φ*(M).

ideas.what: For a BT_1 in characteristic p, the Frobenius pullback of the Hodge filtration ω ⊂ M equals Im V = Ker F in M^(p).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of Hodge and conjugate filtrations / Frobenius twist of Hodge filtration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oda (1969) for abelian varieties; Mazur (1972–73); Berthelot–Breen–Messing (1982) for BT groups
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970/74); unsure of the exact statement there

ideas.what: Structure of (M, F, V) for a BT_1: Hodge filtration ω ⊂ M plus conjugate filtration Im F ≅ t'^(p) ⊂ M, with M/Im F ≅ ω^(p) via V. These give Frobenius-linear identifications of graded pieces.
ideas.modern_name: F-zip (Moonen–Wedhorn) / Dieudonné space attached to BT_1; Ekedahl–Oort data

ideas.what: Recovery of the Hasse–Witt type operators V_ω: ω → ω^(p) and F_{t'}: t'^(p) → t' from the Dieudonné module with Hodge filtration, with V_{ω'} = ^tF_{t'} under duality.
ideas.modern_name: Hasse–Witt / Cartier operator on invariant differentials and Lie algebra; duality of F and V

ideas.what: Question whether (𝓜, F, V) alone determines all of data b), i.e. whether the Hodge filtration is forced by F, V.
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness / reconstruction of the Hodge filtration from the Dieudonné crystal mod p
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Jong (1993, 1995) for full faithfulness over nice bases; Berthelot–Breen–Messing

missed.claim: Grothendieck writes down, for BT_1 over an arbitrary characteristic-p base, the combination 'Hodge filtration + conjugate filtration + Frobenius-semilinear identification of graded pieces' (continued as the cross diagram on p.13). This is essentially the notion of an F-zip, formalised only by Moonen–Wedhorn in 2004 and underlying Ekedahl–Oort stratifications.
missed.quote: φ*(ω) ne soit autre que Im(M →V_M M^(p)) ... t'^(p) = Coker(M →V_M M^(p)), donc F_M : M^(p) → M se factorise par t'^(p) ↪ M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical priority. It shows the F-zip structure of BT_1 was explicitly isolated in Grothendieck's 1970 crystal programme, linked to his questions on whether such data classify BT_1 over general bases.

missed.claim: The question whether (𝓜, F, V) alone recovers the full data b), i.e. the Hodge filtration, is left open. His uniqueness claim holds only when Frobenius is faithfully flat (regular bases) and fails over non-reduced bases.
missed.quote: La seule donnée des 𝓜, F_𝓜, V_𝓜 permet-elle de récupérer toute la donnée b) ? ... Cela détermine ω de façon unique !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Answered in later literature (de Jong; Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory showing the Hodge filtration is extra data over nilpotent thickenings), so of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard Dieudonné theory of BT_1 (Hodge filtration twisted by Frobenius equals Im V = Ker F). Mildly notable is that Grothendieck explicitly assembles the F-zip-type structure and asks whether it recovers the co-Lie data, decades before Moonen–Wedhorn. But Oda, Kraft and Oort have closely related content, and the uniqueness claim has a gap over non-reduced bases.
transcription_corrections: Margin note reads 'Cela détermine ω de façon unique !' with 'de façon unique' underlined (heavily for 'unique').
In the final line, the image reads 'd'où F_{t'} : t'^(p) ↪ M' followed by a struck arrow; the intended map is t'^(p) → t' after composing with M → t'.
'Signifie que F_𝓜, V_𝓜 forment suite exacte' — the image reads 'forment suite exacte' for 𝓜 and 'forment suites exactes .....' for M.
Bracket: 'ω = H^1(ℓ.[-1]) = H^0(ℓ.), ν' = H^1(ℓ̌.')' and 'n = H^0(ℓ.[-1]) = H^{-1}(ℓ.), t' = H^0(ℓ̌.')'. The prime/check is on the dual complex; the image suggests ℓ̌.' rather than ℓ̌_0'.
